active_themes.label: AI Spending Backlash
active_themes.summary: The sell-off that began 2026-10-30 hit bottom at a Nasdaq close of 22,618, then bounced 6.51% to 24,090 on Monday on Nvidia's one-day recovery. Today the Nasdaq fell back to 23,734 as Nvidia dropped 5% and Anthropic slid below its IPO price, while the Dow and small caps rose. Nvidia is still far below its pre-episode value, the accounting probe is unresolved, and bipartisan objections to Huang's return add a new overhang. The open question is whether the Nasdaq holds well above 22,618 without fresh Nvidia-specific good news.

active_themes.label: Forced Selling Everywhere
active_themes.summary: Gold fell 2.45% to $3,561.90 today, giving back about two-thirds of Monday's bounce from the $3,515.40 low of 2026-11-20. It fell on a day the dollar slipped and yields were flat, so neither explains it, and the likeliest reading is continued cash-raising by investors hurt in tech. Gold and the Nasdaq falling together again keeps the liquidation story alive. A close under the $3,515.40 low would erase the bounce entirely.

active_themes.label: Gulf Oil Slowly Returns
active_themes.summary: Oil bounced today, with WTI up 2.35% to $82.05 and Brent up 2.27% to $91.40, after Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah and an alleged attack on a Saudi refinery. That is the first test of whether threats to output, not just shipping, can reverse the recovering-supply story. Brent is still well under $95, so the market is treating this as a risk premium, not lost barrels. The open question is whether a confirmed outage pushes prices decisively higher.

active_themes.label: Global Borrowing Costs Climb
active_themes.summary: The 10-year yield closed at 4.92% (up 0.01 pts) and the 30-year at 5.29% (down 0.01 pts), essentially flat on a day stocks surged 5%. The bond market did not unwind its safety buying, and it did not add a growth-scare move either. The open question is whether yields drift back toward 5.25% as the panic fades or stay pinned by recession worries.

active_themes.label: Fed Eyes Another Hike
active_themes.summary: Waller's half-point hike idea remains unechoed by any other policymaker. Some forecasters now expect three consecutive hikes beginning next month, and the dollar rose 0.49% to 104.32 as hike bets built. Equities ignored this today. The open question is whether the next inflation reading forces stocks to price the hikes.

active_themes.label: AI Drives Inflation
active_themes.summary: Goolsbee's (Chicago Fed president) and Georgieva's (IMF head) warnings that AI demand pushes up prices and rates, which began 2026-11-19, did not get bond-market confirmation today, because falling yields reflected fear rather than inflation expectations. The thesis is intact but is being overrun by the growth scare. The open question is whether yields rise again once stocks stabilize.

open_watchlist.condition: A Fed policymaker other than Waller publicly says a half-point hike is warranted.
open_watchlist.meaning: The outsized hike is a committee idea and not one governor's trial balloon, so December hike risk rises sharply.
Cheaper fuel is starting to take pressure off inflation, which weakens the case for a big hike.
The AI-drives-rates argument would have bond-market confirmation, which is the sharpest pressure on high-priced tech shares.
Demand for AI stock itself would be fading, so the IPO stops being a side effect and becomes a signal.
The AI sell-off is extending past Friday's drop, which would mean the funding doubt is deepening and not stabilizing.
Fear of economic damage is overpowering the inflation worry, which would make a Fed hike harder to justify and mean the market expects pain from the AI unwind.
A drop of about 9% from today's $165.05 close would show the CEO-return relief is fading while the accounting probe still hangs over the stock.
That would take gold under its prior session's forced-selling low and show the cash-raising phase is resuming rather than ending.
Oil is pricing actual supply loss from the Houthi threats, not just a risk premium, which adds to inflation pressure ahead of Fed decisions.
The quiet rotation has turned into a renewed panic, which would bring back forced selling across assets.
